title: Les Paul & Leo Fender Part II
summary: Part two of the Les Paul and Leo Fender story, covering the origins of the solid body electric guitar. The hosts trace Paul Bigsby's influence and the Merle Travis guitar, Fender's bolt-on neck and single-row tuning headstock, and the Precision bass. They cover Les Paul's 1948 car accident and arm injury, the Esquire and Telecaster (with the Broadcaster name dispute with Gretsch), Les Paul's Gibson endorsement and the Les Paul model, and the Stratocaster's ergonomic design. They also discuss Buddy Holly and Muddy Waters's UK tours, Dick Dale and surf guitar, session bassist Carol Kaye, Leo Fender's sale of Fender to CBS, and Les Paul's later life and honors. The episode ends with a request for reviews instead of listener mail.
topics: Les Paul car accident arm injury

segments.title: Recap and introduction
segments.summary: Josh recaps part one: Leo Fender and Les Paul working on amplified electric guitar feedback, and the arrival of Paul Bigsby.

segments.title: Paul Bigsby and the Merle Travis guitar
segments.summary: Bigsby is known for the Bigsby tailpiece and whammy bar. He built a solid body guitar for country musician Merle Travis, and Leo Fender borrowed it. The hosts describe similarities in the headstock and tuning peg layout, and the lawsuit over the headstock.

segments.title: Precision bass and electric bass
segments.summary: Leo Fender's Precision bass solved the problem of bulky upright basses. Paul Tutmarc earlier built an electric solid body bass. The hosts discuss the bass's role in rhythm sections and in later music.

segments.title: Affordable amplified guitars and bolt-on necks
segments.summary: Fender made electric instruments affordable and mass-produced. He used bolt-on necks, unlike Gibson's glued set necks, and the hosts compare the sound of each method.

segments.title: Les Paul's car accident and arm injury
segments.summary: Les Paul and Mary Ford were in a car accident in Oklahoma. His right elbow was shattered and doctors wanted to amputate, but he chose a procedure that left the arm bent, and he recovered over about a year.

segments.title: Esquire, Telecaster and the Broadcaster name
segments.summary: Fender debuted the Esquire at the 1950 NAMM show and then developed it into the Broadcaster, which was renamed the Telecaster after Gretsch objected to the name. Les Paul rejected a Telecaster sent to him.

segments.title: Gibson Les Paul model and endorsement deal
segments.summary: Gibson, which had turned Les Paul away earlier, was already developing a solid body guitar. The result was the Gibson Les Paul, which Les Paul endorsed for a royalty. The hosts discuss weight differences and Les Paul's credit for the design.

segments.title: Stratocaster and the Flying V
segments.summary: Fender released the Stratocaster in 1954 with contoured edges and horn cutaways for comfort and high-fret access. Gibson's Flying V and Explorer followed, and Fender's Jazzmaster and Jaguar came later.

segments.title: Buddy Holly, Muddy Waters and Dick Dale
segments.summary: Buddy Holly and Muddy Waters toured the UK with Fender guitars, which influenced the British Invasion bands. Dick Dale and surf guitar brought enormous volume, and the hosts mention Carol Kaye and the Wrecking Crew.

segments.title: Leo Fender sells Fender to CBS; Les Paul's later life
segments.summary: Leo Fender sold Fender Music Corporation to CBS after health problems and disputes with Don Randall. Les Paul's career faded, he later played small clubs, and he was inducted into both the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the National Inventors Hall of Fame.
topics: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame

segments.title: Outro and review request
segments.summary: The hosts skip listener mail and ask listeners to leave reviews and ratings for the show.
